content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in the short term, especially when sentiment is bullish.", "Sentiment spikes often precede price corrections, indicating a lag between sentiment and actual price movement.", "Models show mean-reversion bias when prices fall sharply after initial rallies, suggesting underestimation of downside risk.", "High sentiment positivity correlates with forecast overshoots, implying sentiment amplifies model overconfidence.", "Forecast accuracy declines when sentiment is volatile or mixed, suggesting sentiment interaction degrades predictive reliability.", "Models fail to capture sharp downward trends when sentiment is neutral or negative, indicating sentiment-driven price suppression.", "Price corrections after forecast peaks are often more severe than model predictions, suggesting underestimation of volatility.", "Sentiment-driven rallies are frequently followed by model-induced overcorrections, indicating feedback loop between sentiment and forecast bias."]}
